## 2026-09-21 — monday-bravo-postcheck: backfilled #employee-performance; found and fixed stale MTD employee-activity pull

Postcheck found 3 of 4 Monday reports posted (aged-inventory, loan-review, layaway-review, all
~08:11 ET) but #employee-performance missing. Root cause: `comms_engine.py`'s employee-performance
renderer reads the first-of-month-keyed `<YYYY-MM-01>_<STORE>_employee-activity.csv`, and that file
hadn't been refreshed since 2026-09-06 — the native Sunday `monday-pull` agent has been pulling a
rolling 30-day `employee-activity` file (dated by pipeline date) instead, so the MTD file silently
went stale for two weeks. Fixed forward: queued a host job (`bravo_pull.sh employee-activity
2026-09-01 CUL,HAR,LEX,ROA,WAY`) to refresh the MTD file for all 5 stores (succeeded, ~6 min), then
re-ran `comms_engine.py post --pub employee-performance`, which posted cleanly to
#employee-performance at 08:47 ET. **Open gap, not yet fixed:** the underlying MTD-file staleness
will recur every Monday until either the native `monday-pull` agent is changed to pull the
first-of-month range instead of (or in addition to) the rolling 30-day range, or the
employee-performance renderer is pointed at the rolling-window file. Next session touching
`monday-pull.sh` or `comms_engine.py`'s employee-performance path should close this properly.

- **The decisive point: the only job left for it is Time Machine, and Time Machine cannot use a
  TB5 drive.** A backup target is bandwidth-trivial. On this 2022 M1 Max it would run at TB4 speed
  anyway. Roughly $800 is being paid for sequential throughput that nothing in this architecture
  will ever read or write.
This also matches the 2026-09-18 audit's own conclusion — *"hardware is not why the fleet is at
62%. Software gaps are. Buy no more hardware for reliability reasons until the gate is being met."*
The binding constraint is the serial one-VM-one-screen Bravo queue; no drive shortens it.
**Recommended instead:** return it; if the local fast-restore path is wanted, a ~$200 4 TB USB-C
SSD does the identical Time Machine job. Saves ~$600 and keeps the benefit. Nothing was written
to the drive and it was never reformatted, so it is returnable in original condition.

## 2026-09-20 (HARDWARE) — Thunderbolt SSD IS ATTACHED, and it is formatted ExFAT (unusable as-is). Time Machine's 16-day "CRITICAL" was a false alarm and is now fixed.

**THE DRIVE ARRIVED AND NOBODY KNEW.** `FLEET_FREEZE_2026-09-16.md` 0.3 and
`FLEET_PLAN_V2_2026-09-18.md` 4.3 both still read "ordered, not yet arrived." It is attached and
mounted, verified live, not inferred: `/dev/disk7`, **Sabrent SB-XTM5, 4.1 TB, Protocol
PCI-Express, Solid State: Yes**, mounted at `/Volumes/SB-XTM5`. Those two files are now stale on
this point.

**IT CANNOT BE USED FOR EITHER INTENDED JOB UNTIL IT IS REFORMATTED.** `diskutil list` shows a
`Microsoft Reserved` partition plus `Microsoft Basic Data`, and `diskutil info` reports **File
System Personality: ExFAT**. That is the factory Windows format. Consequences, both hard:
- **Time Machine will not accept an ExFAT destination at all** — it requires APFS (or HFS+).
- **A Parallels VM on ExFAT is a corruption risk**: no journaling, no POSIX permissions, no
  sparse-file support. An unclean shutdown mid-write can take the Bravo VM with it, and the
  missing permission bits are their own class of launchd/TCC failure.
Contents verified before saying "safe to erase": **7 entries, all Sabrent factory files**
(`.VolumeIcon.icns`, `.sab.ico`, `Autorun.inf`, `System Volume Information/`, Spotlight/fseventsd
stubs). 15.0 MB used of 4.1 TB. **Zero user data.** Erase is safe; it has not been done — it is
irreversible, so it waits for Joshua's go.

**THE DISK EMERGENCY IS OVER, WHICH CHANGES WHAT THE DRIVE IS FOR.** On 9/16 the internal volume
had 46 GB free. Today: **106 GB free** (Data 349 GB used of 460 GB, 76%). Measured consumers:
Parallels **45 GB**, Claude app support 13 GB, Unified Search 8.9 GB, CloudStorage 177 MB, and
**Bravo Data Extraction output just 58 MB**. So moving the Bravo output — the thing 0.3 was
written to do — would reclaim 58 MB. It is not worth a single line of change. Moving the VM
reclaims 45 GB onto a disk that already has 106 GB free, in exchange for a **new hard dependency
where an unmounted volume means Bravo does not start and the whole morning pull dies.** That is
the wrong trade during a reliability freeze. Board decision: **Time Machine destination first,
cold archives second, VM move only after a mount-gate exists and has proven for a week.**

**TIME MACHINE HAS BEEN HEALTHY THE ENTIRE TIME. THE ALARM WAS THE BUG.** `DISK_HEALTH.md` has
written `CRITICAL ... Could not determine last successful Time Machine backup time` **every four
hours since 2026-09-04 — ~100 entries over 16 days.** Root cause, proven not guessed:
`disk_health_sentinel.py` called `tmutil latestbackup` and nothing else, and that command
**requires Full Disk Access**, which the launchd runner does not have. It returns a permission
message; the regex misses; the sentinel converted *"I am not allowed to look"* into *"CRITICAL."*
Meanwhile the real record: backups completing to the NAS **every ~2 hours all day today**, newest
`2026-09-20 16:12:39` local — **71 minutes old** at the time of the check. Same Full Disk Access
gap already logged for unified-search and ffl-guardian; this is its third victim.

**FIXED (`bin/disk_health_sentinel.py`, backup `.bak-pre-tmhardening-20260920`).**
`tm_last_success_age_hours()` now tries three independent routes and takes the first that answers:
(1) `tmutil latestbackup` (unchanged, still best when FDA lands), (2) the `SnapshotDates` array
inside `defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.apple.TimeMachine` — **no FDA required**, (3) the
dated `.backup` snapshot the destination currently has mounted. Route 2 deliberately reads ONLY
`SnapshotDates` and **ignores `StableLocalSnapshotDate` / `ReferenceLocalSnapshotDate`** — those
are LOCAL snapshots, and counting them would report a healthy backup while the NAS was
unreachable, which is precisely the 8/25 outage this sentinel exists to catch.
**Tested before shipping, four cases:** a fixture whose local-snapshot dates are deliberately
NEWER than the real backup dates (parser correctly returns the older, correct one — the trap that
would have made this fix worse than the bug), empty preferences, an error string, and finally
**live on the host**: route 1 `None` · route 2 `2026-09-20 16:12:39` · route 3
`2026-09-20 13:53:37` · RESULT `1.1 hours ago` · VERDICT `healthy - no alarm`. The 18:00 run is
the first that should come back clean.

**NEW: `bin/storage_diag.sh`** (read-only, allow-listed, sections `volumes|tm|tmprobe|tmcheck|space|big|all`).
Nothing in `bin/` could answer "what volumes are attached, how are they formatted, where is Time
Machine actually pointed" — `host_diag.sh` covers agents/registry/logs only, which is why a drive
plugged into this machine went unnoticed in two planning documents. It never formats, mounts,
unmounts, erases or deletes. Added to `fleet/host_queue_allowlist.txt` (backup
`.bak-pre-storagediag-20260920`) per Freeze Rule 4's documented extension path — a new versioned
script in `bin/`, listed, called by name; the check itself was not widened.

**Also seen, not acted on (one thing at a time):** 7 local Time Machine snapshots accumulated
today; `com.valleypawn.chrome-tab-hygiene` last exit status 1; `com.valleypawn.commandcenter`
status -9.

Freeze-compliant: no new scheduled task, no registry change, no launchd/plist change, no
`fleet/` structural change, no quiesce/relaunch. One backed-up edit to one existing script, one
new read-only script, four read-only host-queue probes.

## 2026-09-20 — FY2026 payroll clearing FIXED: $370K of impossible balances removed from the balance sheet

**JE `PAYROLL-CLEARING-FIX-` posted 09/20/2026: Dr Gusto Clearing 185,000.02 / Cr Payroll
wages and tax to pay 185,000.02.** Verified live — Gusto Clearing **-185,667.48 → -667.46**,
Payroll wages and tax to pay **-200,373.01 → -15,372.99**, net income unchanged, 12/31/2025
re-verified untouched.

**The cause.** Three overlapping payroll recording paths ran in 2026. (1) `GUSTO-PAY-2026-MM`
monthly JEs debited payroll expense and credited **Gusto Clearing** — Jan–Apr only, 229,000.98.
(2) The Gusto ACH drafts out of WF 2797 were worked in the bank feed as *transfers* debiting
**Payroll wages and tax to pay** — 56 transactions, 185,000.02. (3) From 22 May the Gusto app's
own per-payroll JEs took over, debiting expense and crediting WF 2797 directly. So for Jan–Apr
the expense half and the cash half of the same payrolls sat in two different suspense accounts
and neither could ever clear. Both froze the moment path 3 started, which is the fingerprint
that identified it.

Not a plug: same identified population on both sides, amount taken from the registers. The
control that validates the method is that **2025 nets to exactly zero** (454,716.72 each side)
because the earlier TRUEUP-2025 entry did the same job for 2025 — 2026 simply re-created the
problem afterwards.

**Left open deliberately, with reasons recorded:** the residual -15,372.99 payroll liability is
the Bravo GL import mapping store paid-outs to the payroll liability (**fix the import mapping,
not the balance** — a JE would be undone next month); **401K Traditional -117,175.55** needs
Guideline's remittance detail to split employee deferral from employer match and was NOT guessed
at (Gate 3); **Bravo POS Clearing -144,403.86** is mostly September's settlements awaiting the
1 October GL import (it was -950.81 at 31 August); **eBay Clearing -189,029.61** is the one
clearing account that never self-corrects and needs its payout-to-revenue mapping decided.

**Needs Joshua:** seven `Journal #Gusto` entries credit WF 2797 for 55,140.61 with no Gusto debit
at the bank (05/22, 05/28, 06/05, 06/18, 07/30, 09/04, 09/18). Their lines read "Check for
<employee>" — Gusto's wording for a payroll paid by paper cheque, where Gusto does not draft the

## 2026-09-20 (UNIFIED SEARCH - FDA denial PROVEN, not theorised. The guard has now stopped two separate data wipes. Silent-rot bug in the verifier fixed.)

- **Joshua: "fix it you know how."** Everything fixable without a security-settings change is now done. The remaining step is a Full Disk Access grant, which is a system security setting - a session does not make those, whoever asks. It is one click and it is described at the bottom of this entry.
- **THE CAUSE IS NOW PROVEN.** Two nights ran with the 9/18 shrink guard live. `.refresh_attempt.log` for 2026-09-19 04:50 is unambiguous:
  - `mail` - `found 0 messages` against 346,748 indexed -> guard aborted, exit 3.
  - `files` - `found 7712 files (7712 iCloud + **0 mail attachments**)` against 50,407 indexed -> guard aborted, exit 3.
  - `msgs` - `sqlite3.DatabaseError: **authorization denied**` opening `~/Library/Messages/chat.db`. **That string is macOS TCC refusing the open.** It is not inference, not a timeout, not a missing file - it is the operating system denying the read. The FDA diagnosis is now evidence, and the 9/18 "leading cause, not certainty" hedge is retired.
  - `notes` - reached the AppleScript fetch and hung, then the whole chain took `Terminated: 15`, so `reminders`, `gdrive`, `photos` and `stats` never ran at all. **That is why `stats.txt` is still dated Sep 12** - and `stats.txt` is exactly what the verifier checks.
- **THE GUARD HAS NOW PREVENTED TWO WIPES, not one.** 9/18 saved 346,748 mail rows. 9/19 saved those **plus 50,407 file rows**, which would have been rebuilt down to 7,712 - an 85% silent loss of the file corpus that nobody would have noticed until a search came back empty. Verified after both nights: `index.db` mtime still Sep 12 05:02, every table's `max(rowid)` unchanged.
- **WIDER THAN UNIFIED SEARCH - `com.valleypawn.ffl-guardian` is very probably failing the same way, silently.** `bin/ffl_guardian_run.sh`'s own header says it is routed through `vp-runner` "for TCC access to ~/Documents **and ~/Library/Mail**", and `ffl_guardian.py` reads `~/Library/Mail/V10` directly via `find`. The proof above shows `vp-runner` cannot read `~/Library/Mail`, so the FFL compliance agent is reading an empty candidate set and would report "nothing found" indistinguishably from "nothing to report". **Not touched this session** (different agent, freeze Rule 2, one thing at a time) but it needs verifying against its real output, and it is a compliance surface. Logged in the Open Items Register.
- **FIXED - the silent-rot bug, which is the reason this went 8 days unnoticed** (`bin/usearch_verify.sh`, backup `usearch_verify.sh.bak-pre-stalegate-20260920`). The verifier's only alarm was the literal `hardened FAILED after 3 attempts` marker - which the wrapper can only write if it SURVIVES all three attempts. On both 9/18 and 9/19 the wrapper was SIGTERM'd mid-attempt-1, so the status stayed `RELAUNCHED`, no ledger row was ever written, and **two nights of 100% failure were indistinguishable from a healthy relaunch**. A verifier whose alarm depends on the thing it is verifying finishing cleanly is not a verifier. NEW **staleness gate**: it now measures the only thing that matters - how old `stats.txt` is - and ledgers one plain-language row per calendar day once the index is 2+ days stale, independent of how or why any run died. Wording branches on whether the guard tripped, so the row names the actual ask. Rule 16 respected: plain sentences, ledger only, no Slack, no jargon, one row per day not per run.
- **Tested before shipping, six cases, with the BSD-specific `stat`/`date` calls stubbed** (a first harness gave false silence because Linux `stat -f` reports filesystem info, not mtime - the harness was wrong, not the code): current real state ledgers correctly and names Sep 12 - a second run the same day stays silent - the no-guard-message branch reads correctly - a healthy same-day index stays silent - a 1-day-old index stays silent - a missing `stats.txt` reads "has never finished a rebuild" instead of "20716 days". `bash -n` clean.
- **WHAT IS STILL BROKEN AND WHY IT IS NOT MINE TO FIX.** Granting Full Disk Access hands a background daemon permanent read access to the entire disk - mail, messages, every file. That is a system security setting, and a session does not change those on anyone's behalf, including on direct instruction. It is also genuinely 30 seconds: **System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Full Disk Access -> `+` -> Cmd+Shift+G -> `/Users/joshuadavis/bin` -> select `vp-runner` -> leave it on.** `vp-runner` already exists for exactly this purpose - `install_agent.sh` REFUSES any agent that does not route through it, precisely so there is ONE grant target for the whole fleet - so this single grant fixes unified-search AND ffl-guardian AND anything else added later.
- **After the grant, to confirm rather than assume:** run `bash "$HOME/Documents/Claude/Projects/Unified Search/refresh_hardened.sh"` (allow-listed as `usearch_refresh.sh` in the host queue) and check `refresh_hardened.log` shows `MAIL DONE: ~347,000 messages` and a `=== hardened success` line, and that `stats.txt` carries today's date. If FDA on `vp-runner` does NOT clear it, the fallback is to run this one job back through an FDA-capable path rather than re-litigating the 9/17 native migration - the other ten agents from it are unaffected.
- Freeze-compliant: one backed-up edit to one existing script, logged here. No new task, no registry change, no launchd/plist change, no `fleet/` structural change, no host-queue job dropped, no quiesce.

Now routed through `bin/vp_slack.py`, which does `conversations.open` against Joshua's USER id, and which also brings the publication receipt and the publish guard for free instead of being a fourth private copy of "send a Slack message". **Verified live: DM delivered to `D0BKWHP503C` with a receipt** — `compliance-brief 2026-09-19T16:00:08 slack-dm -> D0BKWHP503C ok`.

A guard that fires on correct code is the same false-alarm disease being fixed everywhere else, so it now requires the id — or a constant bound to it — to be USED as a channel value on a non-comment line. ## 2026-09-19 (THE SANDBOX — prove the monitoring works in seconds instead of waiting a week. Then prove the proof.)

- **Joshua, verbatim:** *"we should be able to sandbox everything, test in a simulated environment, and know production is reliable."* Correct, and the reason it matters: waiting seven days to learn whether a detector works is not a test, it is a hope — and the conditions that matter (corrupt state, a deleted script, six reports failing the same morning) only occur during a real outage, which is exactly when you cannot afford to be debugging the thing meant to catch it.
- **NEW `bin/fleet_sim.py` — a throwaway HOME, real faults planted on purpose, the REAL scripts run against it.** `bin/` is **symlinked, not copied**, so the suite can never drift into testing a second version of the code nobody runs. Fixtures: fake `Library/Logs/valleypawn`, fake `Library/LaunchAgents`, synthetic plists and logs, a manifest and Tier-1 file. Production is never touched. **32 scenarios, all green.**
- **Every scenario encodes a real bug or false alarm from 9/18–9/19**, so none of them can silently come back: weekly agent idle 4 days is not stale · daily agent quiet 40h is · an old `.err.log` is health, not fault · "FAILED WAY" is a store code · `REFUSED` in the host queue is the allow-list working · a tail crash is still-failing but an earlier-and-fixed one is resolved · the retirement tool refuses a live agent · the allow-list refuses the env-prefix smuggle · the publish guard expires on read, has a ceiling, keeps diverted sends out of the real receipts, and fails OPEN.
- **THEN THE SUITE WAS TESTED AGAINST ITSELF — `--mutate`.** 32 green proves nothing if the checks cannot fail. Mutation mode re-introduces each fixed bug into a **copy** of `bin/` and requires the named check to go red. **First run: 4 caught, 2 SURVIVED.** Two of the 32 checks were decorative — they passed with the bug reinstated:
  - the benign-filter check inspected a sliced string rather than the actual count;
  - the state-shadowing check **grepped the source** for `tstate`, which still appeared elsewhere.
  Both were rewritten as **behavioural** assertions: read benign.log's own problem count out of the table and require 0; and actually RUN the scorecard against the sandbox and require its state file to survive as a `dict`. Added `--sim` to `field_scorecard.py` (suppress the DM like a dry run, but still persist state) purely so behaviour can be asserted instead of source-grepped. **Source-grepping is a weak test; this is the lesson.**
- **The mutations themselves were also wrong, and that was found the same way.** Removing the BENIGN filter alone was a no-op because `BAD` had been narrowed in the same sitting; and renaming ONE `tstate` never executed, because the sandbox entry takes the POSTED branch. **A mutation that does not actually reinstate the bug is a false reassurance, exactly like a decorative check.** Both sharpened (restore the over-broad pattern too; rename every occurrence). **Final: 32/32 green, 6/6 mutations CAUGHT, 0 survived.**
- **Wired into the nightly doctor as section 0.** The sandbox now runs first every night at 02:10; a red result is reported as *"the self-test of the monitoring itself did not come back clean, so tonight's results are not trustworthy"* — ahead of every other finding, because if the checks are wrong the numbers beneath them are meaningless. Verified live: report written, DM sent, ledger row, findings correctly dropped 8 → 3 as the scorecard's own crash entries aged out of the tail.
- **WHAT THIS PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT — stated in the tool's own docstring so no future session overclaims it.** It proves the CONTROL plane: detectors fire on real faults, stay quiet on healthy ones, survive corrupt input, and cannot report "clean" while broken. It does NOT prove the DATA plane — whether Bravo's UI stalls tomorrow is a property of Bravo, not of this code. **A green run means: if production breaks, we WILL be told. It does not mean production will not break.**
- Allowlist: +`fleet_sim.py`. All files `py_compile` / `bash -n` clean.

## 2026-09-18 (HARDENING — the watchdog had been dead for an unknown length of time, and an agent had been failing hourly since August. Both found, both fixed, both now self-checked nightly.)

- **THE WATCHDOG WAS DEAD. Root cause found, not guessed.** `field_scorecard.py` — the fleet's own Tier-1 watchdog — crashed with `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'setdefault'` on **every run**. Cause: in the TODAY-view loop the loop variable was named `state`, **shadowing the persistent state dict**; after the loop `state` held a string like `"POSTED"`, and `save_json_atomic(STATE, state)` then wrote that string into `field_scorecard_state.json`. So each run corrupted its own state and the next run died on it. **A crashed watchdog raises no alarm about itself** — which is precisely why the 8/17–8/20 and 9/12–9/17 outages ran for days with nobody told. Renamed to `tstate` (with a comment saying never rename it back).
- **`load_json()` hardened against the same class.** Valid JSON of the WRONG SHAPE was the killer: `json.load()` returns a `str` quite happily, so the existing try/except never fired. Now the shape is checked against the default's; a mismatch is logged, the bad file is moved aside as `.corrupt-<stamp>`, and the run continues clean instead of dying.
- **NEW fleet-event alarm in `field_scorecard.py`.** 5+ unrelated Tier-1 tasks missing TODAY is now reported as **ONE outage, not N late reports** — with plain-language wording that says a shared dependency is likely down, and **escalation by day** ("Day 3: this has been going on since…") rather than the same line every morning. One ledger row, one DM per day of the event, never one per task. Directly targets the six-day blindness.
- **Proven before it was needed: `--simulate-fleet-event`.** An alarm nobody has watched fire is not a control. The rehearsal forces the condition with real task names, DMs nothing, marks its ledger row SIMULATED, and **resets its own state afterwards** — otherwise the rehearsal would suppress tomorrow's real day-1 alert as a duplicate, i.e. the test would silence the alarm it was meant to prove. Verified: alarm fired, wording correct, state reset, file confirmed to be a dict again.
- **NEW `bin/log_triage.py`** — reads every native heartbeat log for crashes AND for staleness, because **a silent agent looks identical to a healthy one from outside**. 69 logs triaged. Found: `dashboard-data-collector` failing constantly, `chrome-extension-watchdog` failing since 9/17, `compliance-brief` dead since 9/14 on `channel_not_found`.
- **NEW `bin/agent_doctor.py`** — cross-checks all 35 launchd agents against the program each actually runs. Found **`com.valleypawn.dashboarddatacollector` firing EVERY HOUR at :20 against a script whose entire task folder had been deleted** — 24 failures a day, 278 error lines, since the fleet diet. It looked healthy in `launchctl list` and in the registry; only stat-ing the target reveals it.
- **NEW `bin/retire_agent.sh`, with a hard safety invariant** — it re-derives the target from the plist itself and **REFUSES to retire any agent whose program still exists**. Both now filtered. (5) "problems in 7 days" could not distinguish *failing now* from *failed and fixed* — added `still_failing`, which asks only whether the END of the log shows a problem. (6) That first flagged two `.err.log`s whose only traceback was weeks old, printing the self-contradicting "STILL FAILING (0 problem lines)". (7) `retire_agent.sh --archive-logs` archived **0 files and reported success**, because it guessed log names from the label — `com.valleypawn.dashboarddatacollector` logs to `dashboard-data-collector.err.log`. Now derived from the archived plist; guessing is refused outright.
- **(8) THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE, AND IT WAS MINE.** `log_triage.py` crashed with `UnboundLocalError`, produced no output — **and `fleet_doctor.sh` printed "clean — no DM."** A broken diagnostic read as a healthy fleet: the exact failure being fixed tonight, reproduced in the tool built to fix it. Two structural repairs: every sub-tool now runs through `run_tool()`, and a non-zero exit is reported **louder than any finding** ("the all-clear cannot be trusted"); and the doctor now parses a stable `SUMMARY still_failing=N …` contract line from each tool instead of **grepping their prose** — because when the wording changed, the old pattern silently matched nothing and turned a wording change into good news.
- **Verified end to end after every fix:** `field_scorecard.py` runs clean twice consecutively with a valid dict state file; triage reports `SUMMARY still_failing=8 resolved=2 stale=4 logs=68`; `agent_doctor` reports `broken_vp=0 broken_other=1 healthy=34` (the one remaining is third-party "Bark", not ours — deliberately excluded from the alarm); and the doctor correctly **DM'd and ledgered** rather than reporting clean. `preston-watch` and `github-backup` correctly moved to *resolved* — both were fixed on 9/17–9/18 and the tool now says so instead of re-reporting them.
- **Still genuinely failing, carried forward:** `chrome-extension-watchdog` (not on bridge since 9/17), `compliance-brief` (`channel_not_found` on its 9/14 weekly run), and the three daily reports' 9/17 "Slack refused the post" (their 9/18 runs succeeded).
- Allowlist additions: `state_shape.py`, `log_triage.py`, `agent_doctor.py`, `inspect_path.py`, `retire_agent.sh`, `fleet_doctor.sh`. All `py_compile` / `bash -n` clean.

## 2026-09-18 (THE GATE — 60% of every miss in the fleet's history lands on 17 dates. It was never 26 broken tasks.)

- **NEW `bin/fleet_gate.py`** — applies the FLEET_PLAN_V2 gate (>=95% delivery, <=1 consecutive miss, 0 accuracy incidents, verifiable, testable) mechanically to `vp_audit.py`'s own numbers. Deterministic: same input, same verdict. A verdict reasoned out in a session is not reproducible and was never going to hold up.
- **THE FINDING — correlated fleet events.** `fleet_events()` counts, per date, how many *unrelated* tasks missed at once. **151 of 250 recorded misses (60%) fall on 17 dates with 5+ simultaneous misses.** 9/14 alone took out **23 tasks** — more damage to the fleet's numbers than every task-specific defect combined. Windows: **9/12–9/17** (the osascript outage, root-caused 9/17), **8/17–8/20** (a second multi-day event, **cause not yet confirmed — stated as unknown, not guessed**), and scattered single days, several of them Mondays (consistent with the Monday Bravo combined run cascading downstream).
- **ELEVEN TASKS ARE AT 100% once shared-outage dates are removed** — weekly-timekeeping-analysis (33.3%→100%), review-obtained-last-week (57.1%→100%), weekly-markdown-verification-review, layaway-yield-weekly, monday-bravo-combined-compile, weekly-store-kpis, nics-weekly-mtd-ranking, monday-bravo-postcheck, daily-unopened-email-eval, weekly-returns-summary, chekkit-unanswered-alert. **Every miss they have ever recorded happened on a day the infrastructure was down. They were never flaky.** Any plan listing them as 11 separate repairs was 11 units of wasted work — the single most important correction in this review. `dark_dates` retention raised 12→60 so the correlation could be computed at all.
- **The REAL repair list is 11 daily tasks** still under the floor after removing every shared date: cloudcover 48.7%, pawn-walk 50.0%, jewelry-onhand 63.6%, items-to-price 70.8%, dress-code 76.5%, discount-review 79.2%, fleet-guardian 79.2%/92.0%, chekkit-eod 84.0%, clock-in 86.1%, sold-review 88.0%, funds-verification 88.4%. **Every one is a DAILY task — the weekly tier has no task-specific defect at all.**
- **RETIRE LIST: EMPTY — and the tool was fixed rather than the verdicts hand-waved.** The first gate run recommended retiring 4 tasks; all 4 were wrong. `bonus-month-close-pull` scored 0/1 and was labelled "has never worked" when it HAD worked, six days late — off-schedule is not absent. The other three had 1–2 expected instances, some inside outage windows. Gate now: a task that produced late is REMEDIATE, and retirement requires **3+ instances** — below that it returns NO EVIDENCE and says to watch it. **A recommendation to delete has to clear a higher bar than a recommendation to fix.**
- **Zero tasks pass the gate today, and that is not the indictment it looks like:** every task's 60-day window contains the 9/12–9/17 outage, and the ceiling is 1 consecutive miss. Nothing running in mid-September can pass, however healthy it is now. Stated plainly rather than presented as "the whole fleet is broken."
- **Next action is a CLEAN MEASUREMENT WEEK** — 7 consecutive days with no infrastructure event — then re-run the gate. That is the first moment a GO verdict can mean anything. The 11 daily defects are real work that does not depend on it. Findings written to `fleet/GATE_FINDINGS_2026-09-18.md`; raw table `fleet/audit.json`. Allowlist: +`fleet_gate.py`.

## 2026-09-18 (ISOLATION TESTING — the whole fleet can now be exercised without publishing to the field. Plus a real hole closed in the host allow-list.)

- **Joshua's ask, verbatim:** *"we should be able to test everything and see if it's working in isolation without publishing a bunch of bullshit to Slack."* Until today the only thing testable in isolation was `daily_report.sh --render` (3 of 48 publications). Everything else could only be tested by letting it post to store managers and team channels — which is not a test, it is a message your staff acts on.
- **NEW `bin/vp_dryrun.py` — the fleet publish guard.** `on` / `off` / `status`. While armed, a task runs completely for real — same pull, same compile, same message text — and the publication diverts to `fleet/test_output/<task>-<surface>-<stamp>.txt` instead of Slack.
- **The dangerous failure mode is leaving it armed**, so it cannot be left on by accident: it ALWAYS carries an expiry (default 2h, hard ceiling 24h) which is enforced **on read**, so a forgotten flag disarms itself; `vp_audit.py` prints a loud banner while it is active so a diverted run can never be misread as fleet failure; and a diverted send is written to a SEPARATE dry-run ledger, never to the real receipts — an isolation test can never masquerade as evidence that a task delivered.
- **Enforced vs honoured — stated plainly, not papered over.** Native scripts are **ENFORCED**: they all publish through `vp_slack.py`, which now intercepts every `post` and `upload` at that one chokepoint. Cowork tasks publish through the Slack connector and have no chokepoint, so for them the guard is an **instruction** — added by `bin/install_dryrun_check.py` as a mandatory precondition block to all **45 Tier-1 SKILLs** (applied, backed up, idempotent — re-run confirms 45 already / 0 written). `vp_slack.py`'s interceptor deliberately **fails OPEN**: if the guard cannot be read, a real publication still goes out, because a publication silently swallowed by a broken guard is a worse outcome than one extra Slack post.
- **Verified end to end on the host, in one run:** guard off → armed → a **real DM to Joshua was attempted and diverted to a file, never sent** → the audit printed the DRY RUN banner → disarmed → a real send went through normally (ts `1789765479.036269`). The one Slack message this produced was the intentional confirmation DM.
- **SECURITY — hole found and closed in `bin/host_queue_run.sh`.** The self-test was refused for using `export`, which is correct. Investigating that refusal exposed a genuine bypass: the allow-list matched `VAR=value` and `continue`d, so a line like `VP_TASK=x python3 /tmp/anything.py` was read as a variable assignment and **skipped script validation entirely** — it would have run any binary on the host. Now only a BARE assignment is accepted (fully-quoted value, since these paths contain spaces, or an unquoted value with none); a variable prefix carrying a command is refused. Proven both ways against the real validator: our actual job lines still ACCEPTED, the smuggle REFUSED. This hole existed since the allow-list shipped 2026-09-16.
- Allowlist additions: `vp_dryrun.py`, `install_dryrun_check.py`. All files `py_compile` / `bash -n` clean.

## 2026-09-18 (MEASURABILITY — every Tier-1 publication can now be audited. 14 blind spots → 1.)

- **The problem, stated plainly.** 14 of 48 Tier-1 publications were unmeasurable: they land in Joshua's DM or in a Slack canvas, and the ops bot cannot read either (a bot cannot read another app's DM, and a canvas has no message history to search). For those tasks "it ran and delivered" and "it never ran" looked **identical from outside**. That is why the fleet could sit at ~62% median delivery with nobody able to say which half was real — and it is why four separate wrong reports went to Joshua this week.
- **Bonus first, because it moves money and was the least visible thing in the fleet.** Before asserting anything: `out/2026-09/` is empty **by design** — `bonus_engine.py` L76 writes `out/<month>/` only at *close*, and September closes Oct 10. **September targets exist** (`data/2026-09/targets.json`, generated 09-09 from the rebuilt sheet: CUL $63,239 · HAR $53,804 · ROA $47,629 · LEX $27,444 · WAY $41,335). No money gap. Verified in code before saying so, per the four premature conclusions this week.
- **NEW `bin/vp_receipt.py` — the publication receipt.** Append-only JSONL at `fleet/receipts/<task>.jsonl`, one line per publication: task, timestamp, surface, target, ok, note. Surface-independent, so DM / canvas / channel tasks are all scored the same way. A receipt is evidence of a **send**, not of correctness — where a channel is readable the channel stays the source of record (Rule 19); the receipt is authoritative only where no readable surface exists.
- **`bin/vp_slack.py` now writes receipts automatically** on every `post` and `upload`, success **and** failure, keyed off `$VP_TASK` (exported by `vp_lib.sh` as the agent name). Best-effort by construction — a receipt failure can never take down a real publication. Every native agent gained receipts with no per-task work.
- **`bin/vp_audit.py` — three upgrades.** (1) New `output: "receipt"` mode. (2) **FILE entries are now scored ON-TIME, not merely present**: an artifact counts only if its mtime falls inside `[instance, instance+grace]`; one that exists but was written outside its window is counted `late` (backfilled), not a hit — because a task that never fires on its day must not look healthy forever (Rule 12). (3) New `{PREV-YYYY-MM}` placeholder for close-cycle artifacts that run on day N and write the month they just closed.
- **`fleet/expected_outputs.json` — 13 entries re-pointed** (additive: old values kept as `_former_output` / `_former_channel_id` / `_former_canvas_id`, each with a dated `_corrected_2026-09-18` note). 2 bonus entries → `file`; 11 DM/canvas entries → `receipt`.
- **NEW `bin/install_receipt_step.py`** — appends the mandatory receipt step to every receipt-scored SKILL.md. Idempotent, backs up before every write, refuses to guess: reports any task whose manifest name does not match its `Scheduled/` folder instead of creating one. Dry-run first: all 11 SKILLs located, canvas ids recovered correctly. **Applied: 11 written, 0 missing.** Re-run confirms 11 already-present / 0 written.
- **WHAT THE NEW MEASUREMENT IMMEDIATELY FOUND — the bonus close cycle has run on schedule once in three.** `bonus-month-close-pull` **0/1**: August's `slack_targets.txt` exists but was written **09-07**, not on its 09-01 run. `bonus-month-close` **1/2**: the 09-10 close landed inside its window (10:55), the 08-10 close did not — `out/2026-07/` was written **09-10**, a month late. Consistent with `RUN_LOG.md`, which still shows July's $1,032 Roanoke payout unpaid in Gusto. This was invisible before today because file *existence* was being read as success.
- **Remaining blind spot: 1, down from 14** — `precious-metals-settlement-handler` (undated `state.json`, rewritten in place; per-run history genuinely unrecoverable). The other 11 read `AWAITING RECEIPTS`, which the audit states explicitly is **missing evidence, not a missed publication**, and each clears on its next run.
- Verified in isolation on the host via the allow-listed job queue — **three read-only runs, nothing published to Slack.** `vp_receipt.py` round-trips; the audit re-run proves the re-pointed entries score. Allowlist additions: `vp_receipt.py`, `install_receipt_step.py`. All files `py_compile` / `bash -n` clean; manifest re-parsed (88 entries).

## 2026-09-18 (UNIFIED SEARCH - near-miss: the nightly rebuild was one un-killed process away from erasing 346,748 mail rows. Shrink guard shipped.)

- **Joshua asked only "is unified-search up to date, I think we automated it."** Answer: **it is automated, it is NOT up to date, and last night it came within a SIGTERM of destroying the index.** Verified against output, never run records (Rule 12).
- **Staleness:** last successful full rebuild **Sat Sep 12 04:13:44 EDT** - the last `=== hardened success` marker in `refresh_hardened.log` and the last `stats.txt` write; the `meta` epochs agree. The index is **6 days old**. Sep 13-17 = the fleet-wide osascript outage root-caused on 9/17 (already ledgered 9/17 04:56 by a prior session).
- **Live counts in `index.db` (max rowid, read-only): mail 346,748 - files 50,407 - msgs 63,509 - reminders 1,964 - photos 4,235 - doc-photos 2,749 - gdrive 459 - notes 87.** The index is INTACT.
- **Last night, the first unattended night on the native agents:** `com.valleypawn.usearch-refresh` (03:30) left **no** attempt line in `refresh_hardened.log`; `com.valleypawn.usearch-verify` (04:50) correctly detected that and relaunched. The relaunched run's mail step printed **`found 0 messages`** and was then `Terminated: 15`. Both plists exist and route through `vp-runner` correctly.
- **THE NEAR-MISS (the real finding).** `usearch.py index_mail()` runs `DELETE FROM mail` **and COMMITS it before inserting anything**. A source that is merely *unreadable* - not empty - therefore destroys the corpus silently, because `os.walk` on a TCC-denied directory yields nothing and raises nothing. Last night's `found 0 messages` would have wiped all 346,748 rows; it survived **only** because the process was killed before the DELETE committed. Proven, not assumed: `index.db` mtime is still Sep 12 05:02 and `max(rowid)` on every table matches the Sep 12 counts. The same DELETE-then-insert pattern exists in all six indexers (`usearch.py` mail/files/gdrive, `msgindex.py`, `notesindex.py`, `remindersindex.py`).
- **FIXED - `shrink_guard()` (additive; backups `usearch.py.bak-pre-shrinkguard-20260918`, `msgindex.py.bak-pre-shrinkguard-20260918`).** Before any destructive rebuild the scan count is compared to the last recorded count in `meta`. A scan of **0**, or under **50%** of what is indexed (`USEARCH_SHRINK_FLOOR`), **aborts before the DELETE** and exits **3** - so `refresh.sh` marks the step FAILED, the hardened wrapper retries, and `usearch-verify` ledgers it, instead of the corpus disappearing quietly. Growth and mild shrink pass through untouched; a first build with nothing recorded is never blocked; a genuine shrink is forced with `USEARCH_ALLOW_SHRINK=1`. Wired into mail, files, gdrive and msgs. `index_gdrive()` additionally restructured so a missing or empty cache file can no longer wipe the corpus and record count 0 - it counted lines *after* deleting.
- **Verified end-to-end before shipping, in throwaway `HOME`s - the real `index.db` was never opened writable** (confirmed unchanged afterwards): 0-found blocks and leaves rows intact - 35%-found blocks - 86%-found allows - growth allows - first build allows - override wipes as asked - CLI exits 3 - a healthy gdrive cache ingests normally - msgindex blocks on a readable-but-empty `chat.db`. A **first draft of the guard silently did nothing** because it queried `meta(key,value)` when the real schema is `meta(k,v)`; the test caught it, not review. Both files `py_compile` clean.
- **STILL OPEN - needs Joshua, cannot be done from a session (Open Items Register 2026-09-18).** Mail indexing has **never once succeeded from launchd**: every Aug launchd-era run logged `Operation not permitted` (which is what the 8/21 move to the osascript path was for), and the first native run logged `found 0 messages`. Every successful rebuild in this index's history ran under Claude.app, which holds Full Disk Access. Reading `~/Library/Mail` and `~/Library/Messages/chat.db` requires FDA and **`/Users/joshuadavis/bin/vp-runner` does not have it** - a GUI-only grant no agent can perform. Stated as the leading cause, not a certainty; the host proof is one `ls ~/Library/Mail` run through `vp-runner` from a launchd context. Until FDA is granted to vp-runner (System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Full Disk Access), the nightly native rebuild will trip the guard every night and the index will keep ageing - **safely** now, but ageing.
- Freeze-compliant: two defect fixes in existing files with backups, no new task, no registry / launchd / `fleet/` / host-queue / SKILL.md change, no quiesce.

## 2026-09-17 (eBAY — RULE 4 added: precious metal is never repriced; Best Offer revert staged; amended policy drafted)
- Joshua, same day, second round of store feedback: *"the managers are saying that they are pricing things at lowest possible for things like silver etc etc, so we likely shouldn't be repricing anything precious metals."* Metal is priced at or just above melt at intake, so there is no retail margin for a markdown to eat — a 10% cut sells the metal under its own value, and the cuts stack to 30%.
- **New shared module `engine/ebay_precious.py`** (pure, stdlib, self-testing). Wired into `engine/ebay_rules.py` (metals get a new `aged_metals_review` FLAG at 90/150 days instead of a cut — they are still aged and surfaced, never silently parked, and photo/specifics/title checks still run on them) and into `ebay_markdown_engine.py`, which now **fails closed**: it refuses to run at all if it cannot import the detector, because skipping a month of markdowns is recoverable and selling gold under melt is not. The engine also now keeps an untruncated `full_title` — it previously cut titles to 55 chars, which would have hidden a trailing `2.1dwt`.
- **Detection was the hard part and was built empirically against all 459 live listings, not from intuition.** A keyword match on gold/silver is wrong in BOTH directions. Correctly NOT metal: `Gold Label` McFarlane figures, a `Platinum Edition` Batman toy, `Vionic ... in Gold Size 10M` shoes, Trifari/Napier `Gold Tone` costume jewelry, a `Gold- toned` Bulova case, `14K Gold Plated` chain, an Auto Meter tachometer whose `10k` is RPM, and a Citizen watch whose model is `E110-K1675`. Correctly metal despite their categories: real sterling filed under *Kitchen* (Reed & Barton flatware ×6), *Collectibles* (a $2,499 VMI sterling medal) and *Fashion Jewelry* (Pandora `925 Silver 11.3dwt`), plus `Charm14K ... 2.1dwt` with no space before the karat mark. **Category is useless in both directions; the fineness/weight mark in the title is the signal** (`sterling`, `.925`, `.999`, `14K`, `dwt`, `troy oz`, `bullion`). A bare karat mark needs a metal word beside it — that is what the tachometer and the watch model taught. Two rounds of testing were needed: the first pass missed three real items and the second introduced two false positives before it settled. Final: 19/19 on the built-in case set, **29 of 459 excluded (6.3%), $10,280.56 of asking value protected**; of the 202 listings already past 90 days, **15 are metal worth $4,420.69** — including a 777-day platinum solitaire at $1,399.99 that was headed for the full 30% floor.
- **Best Offer revert — Joshua said yes.** Staged as one-shot task `ebay-bestoffer-revert-oneshot` (fires 2026-09-17 16:15 ET, self-deletes) to switch Best Offer back OFF on the ~193 Culpeper listings our own August remediation turned on. **Two real hazards were found and fixed in `ebay_policy_fix.py` before staging it:** (1) `--revert` ignored `--only`, so a blanket revert would ALSO have undone the RET30/RETON returns fixes — putting listings back on 14-day or no returns and directly damaging Top Rated Seller standing; `--revert` now REQUIRES `--only` and refuses without it. (2) `--revert` wrote to eBay immediately — `--apply` was only honoured on the forward path — so a bare `--revert` was a live write with no dry run; it is now dry-run by default. The task runs the dry run first, refuses to proceed if any `RET30`/`RETON` line appears or the count is implausible, spot-checks 3 items live afterwards for both `BestOfferEnabled=false` AND surviving `Days_30` returns, then reports in plain language to #ebay-performance and DMs Sandi.
- **Amended policy drafted, NOT yet sent.** `eBay Listing-Age Standard` rebuilt in house format (navy call-out box, three `→` lines, 8pt legal paragraph, 4-column signature block, one page, signature underscores verified non-wrapping). Box reads "Leave the price alone for the first 90 days / Never mark down gold, silver or coins"; effective 2026-09-22; states it replaces the 2026-08-05 version; carries the CEO-approves-the-numbers line. Held at Joshua's format preview per `policy-lifecycle` — Drive copy, #policy-announcements post and the Gusto e-signature push all wait on his yes. Deliberately scoped to repricing only (the Best Offer / video-games rule is a separate policy if he wants it signed).

We do not want make an offer on video games at all. Stop deleting model numbers that appear to be internal tracking numbers."* All three are now encoded in code, in the task prompts, and in the account-level `ebay-context` skill. Freeze-compliant: no new tasks, no registry/launchd/quiesce work, two task prompts edited one at a time through the app's own API, nothing hardened modified in place.
- **Rule 1 — markdowns start at 90 days.** `engine/ebay_rules.py` `AGE_FIRST/AGE_SECOND/AGE_PULL` **30/60/90 → 90/120/150**; queue kinds renamed `aged_30/60/90` → `aged_90/120/150` and the day-30 "send offer to watchers or first cut" reason is gone. The native monthly engine (`~/ebay_markdown_engine.py`, `AGED_DAYS=90`) already worked this way — the rules layer was the thing cutting at 30. Department plan §5 Layer 2 updated. **NOT closed: the signed employee policy still says "Reprice at 30"** — Open Items Register 2026-09-17, needs `policy-lifecycle`.
- **Rule 2 — Best Offer is never turned on; video games never take offers.** The `bestoffer_on` AUTO action is removed from `ebay_rules.py` and replaced with a FLAG-only `bestoffer_on_video_game` (surfaces games we previously switched on, for a person to undo). `ebay_apply.py`: `ALLOWED` is now `("returns_fix", "sku_set")` and the `bestoffer_on` builder returns a no-op — two independent gates, so neither a stale `queue.json` nor a hand-passed `--kind` can enable Best Offer; `--revert` still works. New `is_no_offer_item()` matches eBay Video Games tree 1249 + children and 16 title hints — verified against 8 real title shapes, 5/5 games caught, 0/3 non-games false-positive.
- **Rule 3 — model numbers are never deleted.** Root cause found: `ebay_title_stripper.py`'s `CODE` pattern made the letter prefix **optional** and allowed 3 digits (`\((?:[A-Za-z]{1,4})?\d{3,}[A-Za-z]?\)`), so it deleted `(A2482)` Apple, `(DCD771)` DeWalt, `(MT2500)` Snap-on, `(2236)` Milwaukee — the highest-value search terms in a title. Tightened to `\((?:VAP|VP|VA|CUL|ROA|WAY|HAR|LEX)\d{5,}\)` in both the stripper and `engine/ebay_common.py` `CODE_RE` (whose group(1) still returns the full code — callers depend on that). Prefix list verified against the real 2026-09-06 snapshot, which contains `ROA011853`, `VA5020375`, `VP4023929`. Tested old-vs-new on 9 real Bravo codes + 12 model-number shapes: **0 regressions, 8 model-number shapes rescued.** Tightening `CODE_RE` also stops a model number being written into SKU as a false Bravo link.
- **Task prompts rewritten** (via `update_scheduled_task`, both currently parked by the fleet diet): `weekly-online-store-audit` — Best Offer auto-fix removed, now returns-policy only, runs the script with `--no-bestoffer` and **refuses to run it unguarded if that flag isn't recognised**, and its Step 2 verification now asserts zero Best Offer writes. `ebay-weekly-quality-fix` — points at the corrected stripper, **greps the pattern before running it and refuses the old permissive one**, requires a removed intake code to be carried into SKU in the same revision, bans `<BestOfferDetails>` from every revision call, and now reports how many codes it deliberately LEFT as model numbers so the rule can be seen holding.
- **Verified:** all 5 changed scripts `py_compile` clean; regex behaviour proven by differential test; `is_no_offer_item` proven on real title shapes; `ALLOWED` re-read from disk after edit. Not verified live against eBay — the eBay write tasks are parked under the freeze and nothing was run against the API.
- **Two independent verification passes were run (Rule 12), and the FIRST ONE FOUND REAL GAPS my own pass missed — all now closed.** (a) `ebay_quality_weekly.py` still carried the loose pattern AND its Slack message told managers to remove "intake codes" — so a loose flag here made a *person* hand-delete a model number; pattern tightened and the message now reads "Keep the model number in the title — only our own stock number (like VAP031234) comes out." (b) Same loose pattern in `ebay_listing_audit.py` and `pick_test_delist.py` (flag-only, still tightened). (c) `ebay_policy_fix.py` still held a loaded `BO_BLOCK` reachable by re-adding one line — block deleted, the BESTOFFER branch now `raise SystemExit`, usage line corrected. (d) Department plan §Phase 4 still specced "send-offers-to-watchers at day 21" — struck. (e) **Three title-writing scripts (`ebay_title_revise.py`, `ebay_title_apply.py`, `ebay_toolfix_apply.py`) had no guard at all** — a judgment task rewriting a title could silently drop a model number with no regex involved; all three now run `_dropped_model_numbers()` and REFUSE such a rewrite (tested 5/5 cases: refuses dropping `(A2482)`/`(CECH-4001B)`, allows removing our own `(VAP031234)`/`(ROA011853)`, allows keeping `A2482` with the parens removed).

## 2026-09-18 (ACCURACY FIX — the scorecard now states TODAY separately; three "broken" reports this week were wrong)

**What happened.** Over two messages I told Joshua that `daily-cloudcover-check`, `daily-dress-code-check` and `daily-clockin-check` were broken. All three were running. Verified in #general: clock-in posted 9/17 10:19 and 9/18 10:19; Cloud Cover posted 9/18 10:38 (all 5 streaming); **dress code posted 9/18 10:44:26 — four minutes AFTER I read the channel and declared it "dark since 9/11."** I also repeated a cause the 9/17 cloudcover run invented about itself (a 1Password extension); Valley Pawn does not use 1Password at all.

**Root cause of the bad reporting — one bug, four symptoms.** `FIELD_SCORECARD.md` listed each task's MOST RECENT EXPECTED INSTANCE. For a daily task checked before its run time that instance is YESTERDAY's, so the row read `daily-cloudcover-check | MISSED | Thu 09/17 10:25` — true about yesterday, and read by me as "this task is broken today." Same class as the other misreads this week: Wednesday's Culpeper-only zeros called a pipeline defect, and my own `bravo_relaunch.sh` calling a healthy Bravo dead because it required `dfsvc.exe`. In every case I reported a conclusion before the evidence existed and treated "I don't see it" as "it didn't happen."

**The fix (built, live, verified).** `field_scorecard.py` now computes `todays_instance()` and leads the report with a **TODAY** block whose states are `NOT DUE YET` / `IN GRACE` / `POSTED` / `MISSED TODAY` / `NOT SCORED`, above a header that says in bold: *a task is NOT broken until its window has closed*, and that the historical table below is NOT today's status. Today's first render: 14 POSTED or NOT DUE YET, 1 real miss. It is now structurally hard to repeat this mistake — the answer is on the page instead of being inferred.

**Standing rules from this (apply to every session):**
1. Never call a publication broken unless TODAY's row says `MISSED TODAY` — i.e. its scheduled time + grace has actually elapsed. Check the clock before checking the channel.
2. Never repeat a cause a failed run invented about itself. Ledger rows are the task's guess, not a finding. (The 1Password row is struck.)
3. Two of the four went dark on 9/12 and recovered on their own with no help. Absence during a known outage window is not evidence that a task needs fixing.

**The one real miss today:** `daily-items-to-price` — nothing in #items-to-price since 9/17 08:14 (verified in channel; window closed 12:00). Traces to this morning's pull: Waynesboro's items-to-price got 241 of 247 rows ("Show More" unreachable after 8 stalled passes), so the certificate honestly said `items-to-price FAILED WAY`, and the 08:00 task's fast path correctly refused a short list. Grid-pagination stall = the real defect to fix next.

## 2026-09-18 (first unattended night on the native agents — the Bravo chain ran itself; 3 more silent failures found and fixed)

**PROOF (verified in the channels, not in run records).** With nobody touching anything: `com.valleypawn.morning-pull` fired 06:50, health gate PASS in 16 s, one combined trigger, result at 07:15, certificate `intake-detail CLEAN / sold-discount-detail CLEAN / items-to-price FAILED WAY`, 29 min — all 5 stores of 9/17 (Thursday) data on disk. Then **pawn walk posted 07:15:30** (66 items, 9 flags), **sold review 07:47:04** (77 items, 4 flags), **discount review 08:25:02** (68 items, 27 flags, full 5-store table). That is the first clean automated morning since 9/11. Also OK for 9/17: funds verification, clock-in check, chekkit EOD follow-up, both fleet-guardian passes.

**Three defects found this morning and fixed:**
1. **`github_backup.sh` had never run — bash syntax error every night.** The secret scanner was inlined as a heredoc inside a command substitution (`SCAN=$(python3 - <<'PY' … PY)`); the Mac's bash 3.2 mis-parses that, read the Python as shell, hit the quotes in the regexes and died (`line 45: unexpected EOF while looking for matching '`). `bash -n` in a Linux sandbox (bash 5) passes it, which is why it looked fine. **Scanner moved to `bin/secret_scan.py`** (patterns verbatim, unit-tested both ways: clean diff → CLEAN/0, planted AWS key + api_key → SECRETS_FOUND/1). First successful run 10:29 — **154 files backed up**. RULE: never inline Python inside `$( )` in these scripts; put it in a file.
2. **`bravo_relaunch.sh` cried wolf twice (04:06, 06:36).** Success required BOTH `Bravo.exe` AND `dfsvc.exe`. `dfsvc.exe` is the ClickOnce *deployment* service — it runs only while an update is in flight, and the health gate treats its presence as the update wedge. Requiring it inverts the test. Corrected to `Bravo.exe` running = healthy; dfsvc presence is now just a logged note. Both false rows closed in the ledger.
3. **Five stale OPEN ledger rows** from yesterday's Slack-refusal (the `$SLACK`-string bug + the two channels the bot wasn't in) closed as RESOLVED with what actually fixed them.

**Honest miss:** `items-to-price` WAY got 241 of 247 rows — "Show More" went unreachable after 8 stalled passes, the retry hit the same wall, so the certificate says FAILED WAY. The gate worked exactly as intended (241 < 247−1). Grid-pagination stall = Phase 2 item, not a regression.

**CORRECTION (2026-09-18, after Joshua pushed back — he was right).** An earlier version of this entry said three morning checks were "still broken" and that cloudcover needed Joshua to fix a 1Password/Chrome problem. Both claims were wrong. Verified in #general and #emails-missed:
- `daily-clockin-check` — last good 9/12, **recovered on its own: posted 9/17 10:19 and 9/18 10:19.** Never needed anything.
- `daily-cloudcover-check` — last good 9/11, **recovered on its own: posted 9/18 10:38, all 5 stores streaming.** Valley Pawn does not use 1Password at all; that cause was invented by the 9/17 run and is now struck from the ledger.
- `daily-dress-code-check` — last good **9/11 10:42**; still dark. Real.
- `daily-unopened-email-eval` — last good **9/11 18:05**; still dark. Real.
All four went dark in the SAME 2026-09-12 event, four days BEFORE this session touched anything (first change 9/16 evening). Two recovered without help. The lesson for the scorecard summary: a MISSED row for *yesterday* is not the same as "broken today" — read the current day before telling Joshua something is broken, and never hand him a cause the task invented about itself.

**Clean-day ledger:** 9/17 recorded not-clean (3 missed, 1 unverified) — all three from the list above. The 7-day clock has not started; it cannot until those three are handled.

Do not re-enable them; the native agent owns each one.

Installed through `bin/install_skill.sh` (path-restricted, backs up to `fleet/_backups/skills/`).

Lesson: check the store calendar before calling any zero a defect (now encoded in `vp_lib.sh open_stores`).
- **Two more root causes found while proving the fix (both now handled in `bin/vp_lib.sh`):**
  1. **The recurring "FAIL no-dashboard" wedge is a locale bug, not Bravo.** `bravo_health_gate.sh` strips the UTF-8 BOM from `_recover_result.txt` with `tr -d '\357\273\277'`, which only works byte-wise in the C locale. Under a UTF-8 locale the BOM survives, `^OK` never matches, and a *successful* recover ("OK CUL") is reported as FAIL (visible in the log as `'\ufeffOK CUL'`). Every native call now runs the gate with `LC_ALL=C LANG=C`; first PASS of the day followed immediately (16:27). The hardened gate itself was not edited (Rule 4). Worth checking whether the Cowork/osascript path ever ran UTF-8 — this may explain the 7/22–7/30 and 9/x no-dashboard outages too.
  2. **Console windows over Bravo.** `prlctl exec --current-user powershell` pops a console window on top of Bravo (Windows Terminal was the VM's default console; even with conhost a transient window appears), and UIA then can't see the dashboard. Fixed by (a) setting the VM's default console back to conhost (HKCU\Console\%%Startup Delegation* = conhost GUID — reversible), (b) running all non-UI VM commands WITHOUT `--current-user` (Session 0: no window possible), (c) `bravo_close_terminals` before every health gate. `bin/bravo_screen.sh` (allow-listed) captures the VM desktop to `Bravo Data Extraction/logs/_vmshot.png` so a session can SEE the VM instead of guessing.
- **Proof:** Daily Pawn Walk, Sold Review and Discount Review for 2026-09-16 (Wednesday → Culpeper only) posted by the native agents at 16:31 / 16:35 to #pawn-walks, #sold-review, #discount-review (bot added to the last two). `expected_outputs.json`: sold-review / discount-review re-pointed from DM to their channels (dated `_corrected`).
